newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai central bank to clarify baht remittance ban.
newsitem.headline: Thai central bank to clarify baht remittance ban.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand said it will clarify on Wednesday its measures to stop foreigners from repatriating baht funds obtained from equity sales, a senior official said.

Thirachai Phuvanatnaranubala, head of the bank's Financial Institutions Supervision and Development Department, said Thailand will allow foreigners to hold baht funds derived from stock sales on condition that they are held for reinvestment in the country.
He said, however, that baht obtained from stock sales will not be allowed to be used for settling loans among foreign investors.
The central bank on Tuesday asked bank custodians not to accept transfers of borrowed and unpaid stocks from foreigners in a measure to stop speculators from raising baht.
The central bank also required non-resident investors selling Thai stocks to remit funds in foreign currencies only.
"We agreed that the new measures will reduce trading among foreigners but bona fide investors will not be affected," Thirachai said.
